title: Conformation-Controlled Luminescent Properties of Lanthanide Clusters Containing p-tert-Butylsulfonylcalix[4]arene

synthesis.procedure: H4L (84.8 mg, 0.1 mmol) and Eu(AcO)3·4H2O (40.1 mg, 0.1 mmol) in MeOH/MeNO2 (1:1 v/v, 10 mL) with 0.2 mL of nBu4NOH in MeOH (1.0 mol/L) were refluxed at 80 °C for 1 h. The solution was evaporated to dryness and the white residue was recrystallized from the same solvent to give colorless blocks of (nBu4N)2·1·4MeNO2 over several days. The main text only states that the Eu and Tb dimers were obtained by a procedure similar to that published for the Gd dimer.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Evaporated to dryness; white residue recrystallized from MeOH/MeNO2 to colorless blocks of (nBu4N)2·1·4MeNO2 over several days.

properties.summary: The pinched-cone calixarene is a UV/near-UV antenna. Solid-state absorption of 1 is at 340 nm. At room temperature the Eu dimer shows no luminescence; luminescence is observed at 77 K. Ligand S1/T1 levels used for the dinuclear family (Scheme 1), taken from the Gd dinuclear analogue, are fluorescence at 453 nm (22100 cm-1) and phosphorescence at 468 nm (21400 cm-1) with a shoulder at 457 nm (21900 cm-1). Back-transfer from Eu to the ligand T1 is invoked to explain the weak room-temperature emission.

synthesis.procedure: (nBu4N)2·2 was synthesized in a similar way to (nBu4N)2·1: H4L and the terbium acetate salt in MeOH/MeNO2 (1:1 v/v) with nBu4NOH/MeOH were refluxed at 80 °C for 1 h, evaporated to dryness, and recrystallized. The isolated crystals characterized by X-ray diffraction are (nBu4N)2·2·4MeNO2. Separate numerical amounts and a yield for the Tb analogue are not restated.

properties.summary: The Tb dimer shows strong solid-state luminescence under 365 nm excitation. Ligand absorption is at 340 nm. Energy transfer from the ligand T1 level to the Tb 5D4 level is efficient; the dinuclear ligand fluorescence and phosphorescence levels quoted for this family are 453 nm (22100 cm-1) and 468 nm (21400 cm-1; shoulder 457 nm, 21900 cm-1), estimated from the Gd analogue.

synthesis.procedure: Main text: reaction of (nBu4N)2[Ln2(L)2(H2O)4], Ln(AcO)3·nH2O, and nBu4NOH in a 1:2:4 molar ratio afforded the cubane complexes. SI: 76.5 mg of (nBu4N)2·1·4MeNO2 (0.03 mmol) and 24.1 mg of Eu(AcO)3·4H2O (0.06 mmol) in DMF/acetone (1:2 v/v, 15 mL) with 0.12 mL of nBu4NOH in MeOH (1.0 mol/L) were refluxed at 80 °C for 1 h and evaporated to dryness. The pale-yellow residue was dissolved in warm DMF/acetone (2:3 v/v, 5 mL) and kept closed to give pale-yellow blocks of (nBu4N)4·3·6dmf over several days.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Evaporated to dryness; pale-yellow residue dissolved in warm DMF/acetone (2:3 v/v, 5 mL) and kept in a closed system to give pale-yellow blocks of (nBu4N)4·3·6dmf over several days.

properties.summary: The cone-conformation cubane absorbs at 356 nm and the band tails to 430 nm. The Eu cubane is strongly luminescent. Ligand levels assigned to the cubane family, from the Gd cubane, are fluorescence at 462 nm (21600 cm-1) and phosphorescence at 482 nm (20700 cm-1); T1 lies above the Eu excited level, allowing energy transfer to 5D1.

properties.summary: Solid-state absorption is at 356 nm with a tail to 430 nm. Under the same conditions as the strongly emissive Eu cubane, the Tb cubane shows very weak luminescence at room temperature, together with ligand-based emission similar to the Gd cubane, consistent with back-transfer from Tb 5D4 to the ligand. Both ligand-based and Tb-based emission are observed more clearly at 77 K. Cubane ligand levels are fluorescence 462 nm (21600 cm-1) and phosphorescence 482 nm (20700 cm-1).

synthesis.procedure: No explicit preparation with reagent amounts is given. The cubane is crystallographically characterized in the SI and is used as the reference for ligand-centered emission of the cone conformation.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Crystals of (nBu4N)4[Gd4(L)2(OH)4(AcO)4]·6dmf were measured (Table S1, Figure S3); crystallization conditions are not stated.

properties.summary: The Gd cubane is the spectroscopic reference for ligand-centered emission of the cone/cubane family. It shows fluorescence at 462 nm (21600 cm-1) and phosphorescence at 482 nm (20700 cm-1), red-shifted relative to the pinched-cone dinuclear Gd analogue. Room-temperature ligand-based emission of the Tb cubane matches this Gd cubane spectrum.
